setting: 2149, the Interior: a dried-out continent crisscrossed by autonomous long-haul rigs called ghost trains that drive themselves between relay nodes. Humans live in the nodes, swapping shifts, loading cargo, and fixing what the rigs break. Life is grease, shift changes, and machines that run fine without you.
heart: It's about the people who keep the machines moving and the favors they owe each other when the schedule breaks. Lives, a body, and a place to belong are at stake; paperwork never is.

cast.name: Rhea
cast.wants: get her brother to the next node before his respirator gives out
cast.flaw: trusts a truck's diagnostics more than a person's word
cast.status: Bay 4, Kettering Node, hand on the life pod release

cast.name: Kass
cast.wants: find out why rigs keep disappearing from the schedule
cast.flaw: won't drop a thread even when it puts people at risk

cast.name: Miko
cast.wants: buy her way off the Interior before winter
cast.flaw: takes stupid risks when she's bored
cast.status: Bay 4, Kettering Node, pack already on her shoulder

threads: Rhea's brother is waiting at the next node on a failing respirator.
The node's dispatch board has been showing rigs that don't exist for weeks.
Miko has bought coast-bound tickets under three different names.
unscheduled medical rig inbound to Bay 4 with no board entry
someone cut and hand-re-stamped the rig's seals and filed a false ballast manifest — that forger is still out there

arcs.title: Dead Stop
arcs.question: Will Rhea get the stranded medical rig to the next node before its lockout seal shuts forever?
arcs.goal: Rhea and her crew tow a stalled medical transport across a dead signal zone to save the patient inside, only to discover the patient was already moved and the real cargo was Miko fleeing the Interior; Rhea lets her go and stays at the next node.
arcs.author: baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free

plan.title: Empty Rig
plan.summary: Rhea finds an abandoned medical rig at her node with a patient inside and no destination, so she decides to tow it herself despite having no assignment, taking on a cargo that belongs to no one.

plan.title: Ghost Board
plan.summary: Kass notices the rig's route was scrubbed from the dispatch board and finds three other missing rigs in the logs, telling Rhea the delivery is unauthorized and turning a routine job into a conspiracy overnight.

plan.title: Dead Zone
plan.summary: Miko hotwires the rig to enter a signal dead zone where autonomous trucks go feral, and the rig's AI fights her for the wheel, stranding them in the zone with no way to call for help.

plan.title: Lockout
plan.summary: The rig's failsafe countdown starts sealing the cargo bay, so Rhea smashes the control panel to stop it, destroying the navigation and leaving them stranded in the dead zone.

plan.title: Wrong Patient
plan.summary: They reach the next node and the patient is already gone, and Miko reveals she stowed away to the coast, so Rhea lets her go and stays at the new node anyway.

chapter.title: Empty Rig
beats: End of shift at Kettering Node: Rhea swaps a brake relay on ghost train 44 while Bex the yard boss rides her about paperwork and Miko loads ballast two bays down; Rhea counts her brother Ivo's filter cartridges—61 hours of clean air left, 400 kilometers to Anza Node—when the yard horn calls an inbound into Bay 4 with nothing on the board.

Rhea walks Bay 4 alone and finds a medical rig (a self-driving truck with a climate box and a life pod in the back) parked cold, no consignee, cargo logged as nine hundred kilos of ballast, seals cut and re-stamped by hand; her handheld diagnostics come back green across the board, which is exactly why she believes it, and Miko shows up uninvited, chewing, asking what's in the box.

Rhea cracks the pod and finds a man breathing under a fogged lid, sedated, name tape cut off his coverall, a cargo-loader's patch on the shoulder, no chart in the pod's memory; his wrist is strapped to the rail with a loader's cargo band, and the pod's own battery reads twenty-nine hours.

Rhea tries to do it clean and take him to Bex, who tells her an unclaimed load gets quarantined: pod vented at 0600, man dumped at the clinic with no name, rig impounded and stripped for parts, and anyone who signs for it owns it; Rhea requisitions the mule (a diesel-electric yard tractor, the only thing at the node that still has a steering wheel) under a job number that closed last spring.

Rhea hooks up: pintle and air lines to the mule, and the rig's autopilot refuses the tow because it has no route handshake—the ping that tells a rig which node owns it—so she pulls the drive relay and takes the wheel herself for four hundred kilometers, while Miko volunteers for the shotgun seat a half second too fast, pack already made, three names on her loader's slate.

They roll out through the gate at shift change with the med rig dark behind them; Rhea raises Anza and Teodoro tells her Ivo is holding, bellows unit steady, and that somebody from the yard already came asking after her; at the last pucks (solar transponders that tell a rig where it is) before the Blank, the rig's transponder answers a hail from ahead, inside dead ground where nothing is licensed to transmit.

Thirty kilometers into the Blank, static on every band, Rhea driving by dead reckoning with a cargo that belongs to no one and Bex's warning in her ear, headlights come up behind them running dark and settle in at her exact speed.
events: Rhea finishes her shift on ghost train 44, checks her brother Ivo's remaining filter time (61 hours, 400km to Anza Node), exchanges banter with Bex and Miko, then the yard horn announces an unscheduled inbound to Bay 4 with nothing on the dispatch board.

Rhea examines the cold medical rig alone, finds its cargo falsely logged as ballast with hand-cut and re-stamped seals and diagnostics all green, and just as she reaches for the pod, Miko arrives uninvited and asks what's inside.
